historical_references.reference: Chahatikas were a group of Jain monks who lived in the 11th to 13th centuries CE in India. They were known for their intense devotion to the Jain deity, Chandaka, and were also called Chandaka-bhakta or 'devotees of Chandaka'. They followed a strict ascetic lifestyle, including rigorous self-discipline and renunciation.

Another reference to Chahatikas can be found in the 'Prabandha-chintamani' by Hemachandra, a 12th-century Jain scholar. In this text, Hemachandra describes the Chahatikas as a class of Jain monks who were known for their great devotion to the Jain deity Mahavira, and who wore a special type of monastic robe called a Chhatra. The Chahatikas were also known for their mastery of various branches of learning, including logic, grammar, and literature.
